text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following an avalanche of selling that has wiped A$1.2 billion off its market capitalisation in just three days, the directors of Coca-Cola Amatil, the biggest brand name in Australia, are understood to have held a series of crisis talks yesterday with it parent and major shareholder, Atlanta-based Coca-Cola Company Ltd, on how to deal with the share price crisis. Page 1.

Less than two weeks after the United States threatened to impose trade sanctions over the issue, Britain has added its voice to international concerns that Australia may be preparing to relax import restrictions on books, compact discs and computer softwae, with the British High Commissioner, Sir Roger Carrick, warning that the move could lead to an erosion of copyright standards and would make the Australian market less attractive. Page 3.

According to Australian Bureau of Statistics figures, released yesterday, merchandise imports have risen to their second highest level ever, with a surge in capital goods imports in January providing further evidence the state of the economy is improving. The figures show merchandise imports rose by a seasonally adjusted six per cent last month to stand at A$6.8 billion. Page 4.

Speaking at a conference yesterday, Seven Network chairman Kerry Stokes said the first step to rationalising the pay-TV industry was to eliminate the need to have a different cable system installed for different companies' channel packages. Stokes called or the merger of the Telstra and Optus cable networks in an effort to stem the millions of dollars being spent on duplicate rollouts. Page 23.

New Zealand's Brierley Investments , which already owns 20 per cent of John Fairfax Holdings, is facing an uphill battle to secure sufficient support from Fairfax shareholders to buy 25 per cent of the group without a takeover bid. BIL will seek approval tmorrow from Fairfax shareholders to buy the extra five per cent of the company, which was previously owned by Canadian Conrad Black. Page 23.

After a profit boost from the Paddington mine was offset by a loss incurred at the Tasmanian Henty operation and lower profit contributions from Porgera in Papua New Guinea and Kundana in Western Australia, Goldfields Ltd has again disappointed the market with a 17 per cent fall in its December-half profit to A$3.6 million. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

An Australian Stock Exchange spokeswoman said yesterday the ASX has a "watching brief" over Coca-Cola Amatil stock, which has experienced a dramatic drop in CCA's share price, which has resulted in more than A$1 billion being slashed off its market capitaisation in the past three trading days. Page 23.

As Hoyts Cinemas Ltd assures shareholders it is on track to meet its 1996-97 profit forecasts after posting a first-half net profit of A$13.1 million, the group has announced it is accelerating its A$500 million expansion program by entering its fifth intrnational market with a A$12 million investment in the underserviced Chilean cinema industry. Page 23.

The office of Finance Minister John Fahey confirmed yesterday the Federal Government will decide next week whether to commence immediate discussions with preferred bidders for three Australian airports - Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth - or to call for a second round of bids which could carry the airport sales process into April. Page 23.

Speaking at the launch of the Australian Chamber of Manufacturers submission to the Mortimer Review of business assistance programs, ACM chief executive Allan Handberg warned Australia risks its A$15.5 billion car and pharmaceutical industries offshore ifit further reduces business assistance programs. Page 23.

Ralph Cwerman, the New-York-based procurement director of the United Nations Association of the United States, has revealed that while the UN spends about A$5.2 billion annually on supplies and services, Australian companies have a meagre 0.6 per cent shae of this generous procurement pie. Page 25.

According to a survey of executives in the top 100 listed Australian companies, conducted by investor relations firm Orient Capital, senior executives of Australia's leading companies prefer dealing with overseas fund managers and institutional investors ecause they believe they are better informed than their local counterparts. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

RGC's offshoot Goldfields has no chance of delivering a full year forecast report made during its takeover battle for Pancontinental Mining as it yesterday posted a December half profit of A$3.56 million. A falling gold price and problems at Goldfields' Porgera and Henty mines were responsible for the 17 per cent drop in profits. Page 29.

Coca-Cola Amatil shares have shed A$2.20 and the group's market worth has slumped by almost A$1.2 billion in the three trading days since Amatil unveiled its 1996 profit. There are concerns overseas investors may follow the stampede to dump Amatil shares.Page 29.

Brierley Investments bid to buy the remaining 4.9 per cent of Conrad Black's Hollinger's Fairfax shares was on a knife edge last night as it required shareholder approval for the proposal. Brierley, which has already bought 19.97 per cent of Fairfax from he Hollinger group, was supported by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting but opposed by Fairfax's four major institutional shareholders. Page 29.

Just 10 weeks after its A$12 million float Network Entertainment has slashed its float profit forecast after revealing a A$1.1 million loss for the December half. The profit forecast has dropped to A$2.05 million from the float forecast of A$4.08 million,prompting an Australian Securities Commission examination of the prospectus. Page 29.

Hoyts Cinemas posted a net profit of A$13.1 million for the half-year to January 2 as it revealed plans to continue a worldwide expansion program with four multiplex cinemas to open in Chile this year. Chief executive officer Peter Ivany said the group wa well on track to meet the forecast full-year net profit of A$22 million. Page 31.

Media mogul Kerry Stokes has attacked the Australian pay TV industry structure saying billions of dollars was being lost and a radical overhaul was needed to ensure all Australians has access to the latest technology. Stokes said Optus and Telstra should agree to merge their competing networks, wanting instead an open-skies policy for satellite pay TV. Page 31.
THE AGE

The Hong-Kong-based Kerry Group, controlled by sugar billionaire Robert Kuok, is sitting on a paper loss of A$141 million after paying A$667 million, or A$14.51-a-share, for 8.5 per cent of Coke bottler Coca-Cola Amatil just weeks before its problems weremade public and the share price collapsed. Page B1. --

Following a price-pitched initiative by ANZ yesterday to cut its rates by up to 2.4 percentage points, a plan which will see the bank commit A$1 billion to the small business sector with a banner 7.9 per cent, three-year fixed-rate business loan, the majo banks are under increasing pressure to cut their business loan interest rates. Page B1.

Amid concerns that the May Federal Budget will make further cuts to costly business assistance programs, Australian Chamber of Manufacturers national chief executive Allan Handberg yesterday joined the call from business for a co-ordinated industry policy saying Australia risked losing a key manufacturer in the automotive or pharmaceutical sector if Governments did not take an active policy stance. Page B1.

In a bid to shake off a dull image associated with its industry, KPMG, the Amsterdam-based accountancy and management company which is one of the biggest in the world with offices in 142 countries, revealed yesterday it has signed a deal with Environment arketing, which specialises in placing brand-name products on movie sets as props, to get the KPMG brand into 18 films in the next two years. Page B1.

The Bureau of Statistics yesterday reported a 6 per cent jump in imports, providing further evidence that the economy is gathering pace. After seasonal adjustments imports rose to A$6.79 billion in January, the second-highest month on record with a sizeabe current accounts deficit likely in the bureau's monthly publication of trade balances. Page B3.

Four small Victorian airlines are scrambling to take up Airlines of Tasmania services, which are grounded by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority for serious safety deficiencies. Under a State Government agreement Airlines of Tasmania is sole license holde for intra-state routes, a right expected to end with State Government deregulation some time in the next 18 months with. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
